meanings: collar or sleeve in older usage
explanation:
裾 is semantic–phonetic, with 衣 identifying clothing and 居 supplying the sound kyo. The older dictionary places the word in the opening or inner fold of a garment.

Shirakawa records a broader clothing range than the modern Japanese hem alone: collar, sleeve, lower edge, and overlapping front can all occur in the lexical tradition. A further description concerns fabric projecting or spreading outward, including the ample appearance of a large garment.

The character can also interchange with 倨 for arrogance and with 拠 for relying on something. These are related-word uses, not anatomical features of clothing. Shirakawa's entry distinguishes the cloth-classified word and its garment parts from meanings introduced through other writings of similar sound.

sources.title: Shirakawa, 普及版 字通 — 裾
